source.title: Exploring new ways: Enforcing representational dissimilarity to learn new features and reduce error consistency
source.authors: Tassilo Wald; Constantin Ulrich; F. Isensee; D. Zimmerer; Gregor Koehler; M. Baumgartner; K. Maier-Hein

record.tranche_reason: The study measures representational similarity with LinCKA and related metrics, but tests how deliberately training models to be dissimilar changes that similarity rather than reproducing the original convergence measurement alone.
record.gate_note: The paper reports its own LinCKA comparisons of independently trained and deliberately dissimilar ResNets; those results are recorded below. Output accuracy, Cohen’s kappa, JSD and error-disagreement results are downstream behavioral measures, not measures of the representation convergence named by these claim versions, so they are not rows here. Results cited from other work are not recorded as study findings.
record.test_reason: The study assumes that independently trained models converge and uses representational similarity as a training tool. It deliberately enforces dissimilarity, then reports similarity and ensemble metrics for its own method. Its only measurement of natural convergence is a figure-only baseline: same-architecture ResNet34 seeds on CIFAR10, compared with LinCKA. That baseline serves as a control, not as a test of any version. The layer-dependence rows describe where the regularizer works, not how measured convergence depends on the similarity metric or the inputs, so they do not test V6.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that enforcing dissimilar intermediate representations is a proof of concept. It lowers error consistency (Cohen's kappa) by about 3 to 7 points while largely maintaining single-model accuracy, and it yields higher ensemble accuracy than independent ensembles. They note that the kappa reduction remains slight.
record.recipe_differences: Instead of measuring convergence among independently trained models as in the original convergence work, this study trains successive models with a loss that enforces dissimilar representations and evaluates the resulting similarity with LinCKA.
record.method_sensitivity: The representational-similarity outcome varies with the regularized layer; effects are stronger at intermediate positions and localized around the selected layer or residual block. In sequential ensembles the decrease is less pronounced for later models, and regularizing multiple layers produces a smaller overall decrease than regularizing one layer.

fits_no_version.finding: ResNet34 and ResNet101 can be trained to have near-zero LinCKA similarity to an existing model at intermediate layers. Accuracy cost is small and ensemble accuracy rises slightly. Regularized models are even more dissimilar to each other than to their base model. Early and late layers resist the dissimilarity, and it is confined to the residual block, with similarity rising after downsampling.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The convergence of same-architecture models is not forced by the task. Equally accurate solutions with dissimilar intermediate representations exist and can be found by explicit regularization, though early and late layers are harder to decorrelate.

record.peer_reviewed: Published at the ICML 2023 Workshop on Spurious Correlations, Invariance, and Stability
record.problems: Representational-similarity results are presented in figures without numerical values or uncertainty estimates. The experiments cover ResNets and CIFAR datasets and do not test scale or capability trends.
record.rows_left_out: Output accuracy, Cohen’s kappa, JSD and error-disagreement metrics from Table 1 and Appendix Tables 2–5 were left out because they measure downstream prediction behavior rather than representational convergence. The paper also reports no numeric LinCKA values for the figures.

untested.parts: No scale or capability sweep across independently trained models.
No vision-language models or paired data.
There is no quantitative seed-to-seed convergence analysis. The baseline appears only as a figure, and no shared features or subspaces are identified.
No mapping, stitching or relative-representation transfer is tested. Stitching is raised only as future work.
No interpretable features or circuits are compared.
The final similarity measure for naturally trained models is never varied (LinCKA only). Inputs and OOD data are not varied.
No test of a plateau, or of shared data or objectives as the cause.

record.verdict_notes: Independent-seed convergence is a premise and control here, not a test. The study's results concern deliberately induced dissimilarity, so the reader's V6 links and labels are removed. The reader's V3 'supports' label rested on a figure-only baseline described only qualitatively, so no verdict is given. The deliberate-dissimilarity result is recorded under fits_no_version.

versions.untested_parts: No sweep tests whether alignment between independently trained models increases with model size or capability.
No vision-language models or paired images and captions are studied.
The baseline comparison concerns ResNets of the same architecture; it does not identify shared individual features or establish that the same features recur across architectures.
No mapping, stitching, relative-representation transfer, or unpaired alignment is tested.
No interpretable features, neurons, SAE features, or circuits are identified or compared.

The study varies regularization layer and reports results across datasets and metrics, but does not test neighbour-count settings, out-of-distribution inputs, or a controlled comparison of input sets.
It does not test whether naturally occurring alignment plateaus or whether shared data or objectives cause convergence.
